headline: Readiness verdict is red today — HRV's still below range and sleep debt is building, so today is about protecting recovery, not adding load.
body_state: Fitness 2.0's composite reads 37.4/low, driven by sleep: HRV sat at 37ms (below your personal band) off 6.1h of sleep (score 72), and 14-day sleep debt is now ~25h. Body Battery started the day at 38 (only +37 overnight recharge). TSB is -16.0, and Garmin's own tag says "Productive" — CTL/TSB genuinely sit in the optimal training band — but the recovery layer overrides that: HRV and sleep debt say protect today, not push it.
session: No running-plan session is scheduled today — the long run is tomorrow. The calendar has "Un1t training" (Cardio, 45min) booked. Given the red verdict, treat it as controlled aerobic work: keep effort conversational, not the RPE 6-8 grey-zone intensity Un1t sessions have run at recently. If it can't stay easy, better to skip or shorten it than stack another moderate-hard day on a 25h sleep debt.
recent: Thursday's easy run (planned 7km) was cut to 5.46km at 4:40/km with HR 149 — high for "easy" and a sign fatigue was already stacking; Wednesday's 4km tempo also came in short (5.43km) at 4:48/km, closer to easy pace than the 4:18-4:32/km threshold target. Both read yellow (78% of planned volume). Two Un1t cardio sessions (Aug 11, 13) added moderate-hard load in between. The pattern the week-review already flagged — grey-zone training crowding out true easy — is repeating.
focus: No intensity today — HRV still below range, ~25h sleep debt
Keep Un1t (if done) genuinely easy, not RPE 6-8
